title: Uniform isometric substitution between nearby analytic parameters
statement: Let $k\subseteq H$ be complete fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, and assume that $k$ is algebraically closed (every nonconstant polynomial over $k$ has a root). For $w\in H$ put $k(w)^\wedge=\overline{k(w)}\subseteq H$, the closure of the subfield generated by $k$ and $w$ for the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $u\in H\setminus k$ and assume $r=\inf_{a\in k}|u-a|>0$. If $0<c<1$ and $v\in H$ satisfies $|u-v|\leq cr$, then $v\notin k$ and there is an isometric $k$-field isomorphism $\phi:k(u)^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}k(v)^\wedge$ such that $\phi(u)=v$ and $|b-\phi(b)|\leq c|b|$ for every $b\in k(u)^\wedge$. Isometric means $|\phi(b)|=|b|$, and both fields in the last inequality are viewed as subfields of $H$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2 and its proof, printed p. 48, specialized to algebraically closed k; closed relative bound with c<1, including b=0.

proof.text: For every $a\in k$, $r\leq |u-a|$ by the definition of the infimum. Since $|u-v|\leq cr<r$, one has $v\notin k$: otherwise $r\leq |u-v|<r$. We will repeatedly use the elementary ultrametric rule $|x-y|<|x|\Rightarrow |y|=|x|$. Indeed, $|y|\leq\max(|x|,|x-y|)\leq |x|$; if $|y|<|x|$, the reverse inequality $|x|\leq\max(|y|,|x-y|)$ is impossible.

proof.text: Apply the cited factorization to each nonzero polynomial $P\in k[T]$: write $P(T)=A\prod_{i=1}^n(T-a_i)$ with $A\ne0$ and $a_i\in k$, allowing $n=0$. Since neither $u$ nor $v$ belongs to $k$, every factor at either parameter is nonzero. Thus $P(u),P(v)\ne0$. In particular evaluation of nonzero polynomials is injective at both parameters: if two polynomials have equal evaluation, their difference is zero.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2, printed p. 48, specialized nearby-parameter argument; agent reconstruction because the cited PDF is absent from this read clone.

proof.text: For each linear factor put $q_i=(v-a_i)/(u-a_i)$. Then $|q_i-1|=|v-u|/|u-a_i|\leq c<1$, and the rule of step 1 gives $|q_i|=1$. Set $Q_0=1$ and $Q_j=\prod_{i=1}^j q_i$. Inductively $|Q_j|=1$ and $|Q_j-1|\leq c$, because $Q_j-1=q_j(Q_{j-1}-1)+(q_j-1)$ and the ultrametric inequality bounds its norm by $c$; the base has error zero. The factorization in step 2 gives $P(v)/P(u)=Q_n$. Hence $|P(v)|=|P(u)|$ and $|P(v)-P(u)|\leq c|P(u)|$ for every nonzero $P$. The zero polynomial satisfies the same two assertions directly.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2, printed p. 48, specialized nearby-parameter argument; agent reconstruction because the cited PDF is absent from this read clone.

proof.text: The set of fractions $P(u)/Q(u)$ with $P,Q\in k[T]$ and $Q\ne0$ is a subfield of $H$ containing $k$ and $u$, and is contained in every such subfield, so it equals $k(u)$. Define $f(P(u)/Q(u))=P(v)/Q(v)$. This is well-defined: equality of two fractions at $u$ says $(PQ'-P'Q)(u)=0$, so step 2 gives the polynomial identity $PQ'=P'Q$, which also holds at $v$. The fraction formulas for sums and products show that $f$ is a field homomorphism fixing $k$, with $f(u)=v$. Exchanging $u,v$ constructs its inverse. Thus $f:k(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(v)$ is a $k$-field isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2, printed p. 48, specialized nearby-parameter argument; agent reconstruction because the cited PDF is absent from this read clone.

proof.text: For $b=P(u)/Q(u)\ne0$ set $A=P(v)/P(u)$ and $B=Q(v)/Q(u)$. Step 3 gives $|A|=|B|=1$ and $|A-1|,|B-1|\leq c$. Consequently $|A/B|=1$ and $|A/B-1|=|A-B|\leq\max(|A-1|,|B-1|)\leq c$. Since $f(b)/b=A/B$, this proves $|f(b)|=|b|$ and $|f(b)-b|\leq c|b|$. Both hold for $b=0$ as well. Applying the norm equality to $b-b_1$ shows $d(f(b),f(b_1))=d(b,b_1)$.

proof.text: Apply the concrete-closure extension lemma with $F=k(u)$, $G=k(v)$, the given complete ambient field $H$, and the isometric field isomorphism $f$ of steps 4–5. It gives an isometric field isomorphism $\phi:\overline{k(u)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{k(v)}$ extending $f$. It fixes every element of $k$ and sends $u$ to $v$ because these assertions already hold on $k(u)$. These two closures are exactly the fields denoted $k(u)^\wedge$ and $k(v)^\wedge$ in the statement.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.2, printed p. 48, specialized nearby-parameter argument; agent reconstruction because the cited PDF is absent from this read clone.

proof.text: Let $b\in\overline{k(u)}$, $b\ne0$. By density choose $x\in k(u)$ with $|b-x|<\min(|b|,c|b|)$, a positive radius. Step 1 gives $|x|=|b|$, and the isometry of $\phi$ gives $|\phi(b)-f(x)|=|b-x|$. Therefore the ultrametric inequality and step 5 give $|b-\phi(b)|\leq\max(|b-x|,|x-f(x)|,|f(x)-\phi(b)|)\leq c|b|$. For $b=0$ the assertion is $0\leq0$. This proves the relative bound on the whole completed field, including the endpoint $|u-v|=cr$.
